title: Canary automation for Private VPC control-plane upgrades
creator: Maya Lin
description: Automate canary rollouts of control-plane upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments. Goal: reduce manual intervention and upgrade windows for customer private control planes while maintaining safety via automated health checks and fast rollback. This ticket covers Terraform/IaC module changes, the canary orchestration controller logic, and runbook + verification automation for post-upgrade validation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A Terraformed canary strategy is available as a module option (percentage-based and instance-count modes). 2) Control-plane canaries run automatically and route only a subset of control API traffic for 30 minutes by default. 3) Automated health checks detect regressions and trigger rollback within 5 minutes. 4) Rollout progress, metrics, and final status are emitted to Console dashboards and a designated Slack channel. 5) Implementation has: tests (unit/integration), Terraform plan/regression checks in CI, and documented runbook.
implementation_plan: - Add canary parameters to modules/private-controlplane/main.tf: canary_enabled, canary_percentage, canary_max_instances, canary_duration_minutes, canary_strategy. - Implement orchestration via new k8s operator (private-upgrade-controller) that reads desired version from Terraform-managed ConfigMap and reconciles canary groups. - Integrate controller with release service to publish candidate artifacts and with RBAC checks. - Expand Terraform module outputs to include canary CI job triggers and SSM parameter for bootstrap scripts. - Update CI pipeline: add terraform plan guardrails, and a canary-deploy job that applies canary-only changes to a separate private-state workspace. - Wire health check evaluation library (healthlib) that evaluates control-plane metrics and returns PASS/FAIL/DEGRADED decisions used by controller. - Add telemetry: emit upgrade.step events and canary.health events to Console and StatsD. - Create automated rollback job and playbook.
rollback_plan: - Controller will set canary_traffic to 0% and scale canary replicas to 0. - Terraform apply will revert control-plane image/version to previous release tag from state (using saved previous_version output). - Trigger data-plane fallback rules: route customers on canary instances back to stable pool via smart-routing policy. - Notify on-call, post-mortem ticket auto-created with collected artifacts (logs, metrics snapshots, helm/operator state). - Post-rollback verification runs to ensure control API P95 and error rates recovered within SLOs.
health_checks: - API server P95 latency (control-plane): threshold < 120ms for canary to be considered healthy. - 5xx error rate: threshold < 0.5% in 5m window. - Reconcile loop success rate: > 99.5% over 10m. - KV-cache hit ratio: no regression > 5% from baseline. - Heartbeat metric from each control-plane instance: missing heartbeat for > 2 intervals => fail. - Long tail GC or OOM events: any OOMKill events during canary => immediate rollback. - Integration smoke: create/delete tenant resource end-to-end < 3s median.
terraform_changes: - Module: modules/private-controlplane/main.tf: add variables for canary_* and new resource aws_ssm_parameter or k8s_configmap to publish desired version. - Add workspace convention: <org>-private-<env>-canary for isolated state during canary. - State locking: ensure remote state locking around apply to prevent concurrent full upgrade. - Add acceptance tests: terraform-compliance scenarios to ensure canary flag not toggled accidentally. - Add automated plan validation in CI that rejects changes that remove canary hooks.
verification_steps: 1) Create a canary workspace and set canary_enabled=true, canary_percentage=10. 2) Push control-plane image: v2.4-rc1 to private registry and set desired_version via Terraform. 3) Observe controller create canary ReplicaSet and route 10% traffic. 4) Run synthetic smoke suite against canary endpoints and confirm health checks PASS. 5) Verify Console dashboard shows canary.health events and no SLO regressions. 6) If OK, promote by toggling canary_percentage -> 50 -> 100 with 30m windows. 7) If FAIL, confirm automated rollback occurs and previous version is restored and traffic routed back to stable pool. 8) Collect logs and attach to ticket.
notes_and_decisions: - Decision 2026-03-11: prefer percentage-based canaries vs instance-count by default to support heterogeneous customer clusters. - Decision 2026-03-12: canary duration default set to 30 minutes but overridable per deployment. - Tradeoff: increased complexity in Terraform state and operator lifecycle vs reduced manual toil and fewer upgrade incidents. - Security: operator runs with least-privilege RBAC; SSM parameters for version are encrypted and access-controlled. - Rollout gating: integrate with service-level abnormality detector (slo-detector) for auto-fail.
open_questions: - Should we support dark-launch mode (no traffic, only telemetry) for major schema migrations? - What is safe canary_percentage floor for small clusters (1 instance may equal >50%); need min-instance logic. - How to handle clusters with custom control-plane patches applied by customer? Need pre-upgrade compatibility checks.
